question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [European architectural structure and its location in India]
options: Basilica of Bom Jesus — Old Goa; built by Portuguese (1594–1605), contains St. Francis Xavier's relics
St. Mary's Church — Madras (Chennai); oldest Anglican church in India built by British (1680)
Portuguese Cathedral (Se Cathedral) — Goa; largest church in Asia dedicated to St. Catherine
St. Thomas Cathedral — Bombay; built by the Dutch East India Company in 1718
wrong_fact: St. Thomas Cathedral in Bombay was NOT built by the Dutch East India Company. It was built by the British (East India Company) and consecrated in 1718. The Dutch had no significant presence in Bombay.
explanation: The Basilica of Bom Jesus in Old Goa was indeed built by the Portuguese (1594–1605) and houses St. Francis Xavier's relics. St. Mary's Church in Madras (1680) is correctly identified as the oldest Anglican church in India. The Se Cathedral in Goa is indeed the largest church in Asia dedicated to St. Catherine. St. Thomas Cathedral, Bombay was built by the British East India Company (not Dutch), consecrated in 1718 — Bombay was a British territory, not Dutch.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Colonial architectural landmark and its architectural style/period]
options: Victoria Terminus (Mumbai) — Gothic Revival style, built 1878–1888 by British architect Frederick William Stevens
Fort St. George — Madras; first major British fortification in India, built 1644
Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya (former Prince of Wales Museum) — Bombay; Indo-Saracenic style, early 20th century
Gateway of India — Bombay; built in 1924 to commemorate Queen Victoria's visit to India in 1911
wrong_fact: The Gateway of India was built to commemorate the visit of King George V and Queen Mary in 1911 — NOT Queen Victoria's visit. Queen Victoria never visited India. The foundation stone was laid in 1913 and it was completed in 1924.
explanation: Victoria Terminus (now CSMT) in Gothic Revival style (1878–88) by F.W. Stevens is correct. Fort St. George, Madras (1644) as the first British fortification is accurate. The Prince of Wales Museum in Indo-Saracenic style is correctly placed in Bombay. The error is in the Gateway of India option — it was built to commemorate the visit of King George V (Emperor) and Queen Mary in 1911, not Queen Victoria, who died in 1901 and never visited India.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Colonial-era architectural ensemble and its location/style characteristics]
options: Raj Bhavan, Calcutta — designed by Charles Wyatt, modelled on Kedleston Hall in Derbyshire (Palladian style)
Rashtrapati Bhavan, New Delhi — designed by Edwin Lutyens in classical style with Indian elements; completed 1929
Calcutta High Court — designed by Walter Granville modelled on the Cloth Hall of Ypres, Belgium (Gothic style)
Victoria Memorial, Calcutta — designed by William Emerson in Mughal-Gothic fusion style, completed 1921
wrong_fact: Victoria Memorial was NOT designed in a 'Mughal-Gothic fusion style'. It was designed by William Emerson in an Italian Renaissance style with Mughal elements (sometimes called Indo-Saracenic or White Mughal Renaissance). Gothic is not a defining element of its architectural style.
explanation: Raj Bhavan Calcutta being modelled on Kedleston Hall in Palladian style by Charles Wyatt is historically accurate. Rashtrapati Bhavan designed by Lutyens and completed in 1929 is correct. Calcutta High Court's resemblance to the Cloth Hall of Ypres in Gothic style is a well-known architectural fact. The error is about Victoria Memorial — designed by William Emerson, it combines Italian Renaissance with Mughal architectural elements (white marble domes, chattris), not Gothic. Describing it as 'Mughal-Gothic fusion' is incorrect.
